agent_reasoning: The buggy intro commit added `PBMAC1_PBKDF2_HMAC` but accessed `pbkdf2_param->keylength` and `pbkdf2_param->salt->value.octet_string` from untrusted ASN.1 input without any validation. If an attacker supplied a PKCS#12 file with a keylength exceeding EVP_MAX_MD_SIZE (64), the subsequent `PKCS5_PBKDF2_HMAC` call would overflow the fixed-size `key[EVP_MAX_MD_SIZE]` stack buffer in `pkcs12_gen_mac`, enabling a stack buffer overflow with attacker-controlled length (CVE-2025-11187). Additionally, if the salt field was not an OCTET STRING, accessing `.value.octet_string` would produce a NULL or invalid pointer dereference. The fixed code moves these assignments after the `kdf_md` fetch and adds explicit checks: it verifies `pbkdf2_param->salt` is non-NULL and has type `V_ASN1_OCTET_STRING` before accessing the union member, and validates that `keylength` is present and in the range [1, EVP_MAX_MD_SIZE] before passing it as the key length to PBKDF2.

intro_commit_message:
Implementation of the RFC 9579, PBMAC1 in PKCS#12

Reviewed-by: Paul Dale <ppzgs1@gmail.com>
Reviewed-by: Tomas Mraz <tomas@openssl.org>
(Merged from https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/24577)
pr_description:
This PR implements RFC 9579 support for PBMAC1 in PKCS#12, including the `PBMAC1_PBKDF2_HMAC` function that derives the MAC key using PBKDF2.

Key changes:
- Add `PBMAC1_get1_pbkdf2_param()` to extract and validate PBKDF2 parameters from a PBMAC1 algorithm identifier
- Add `PBMAC1_PBKDF2_HMAC()` to derive the MAC key via PBKDF2-HMAC, with proper validation of input parameters:
  - Validates the salt field is present and has the expected OCTET STRING ASN.1 type before dereferencing
  - Validates the keylength field is present (as required by RFC 9579) and falls within the accepted range (1 to EVP_MAX_MD_SIZE inclusive)
- Update `pkcs12_gen_mac()` to support PBMAC1 in addition to the existing legacy PKCS#12 MAC schemes
- Update `PKCS12_verify_mac()` to detect and handle PBMAC1-protected PKCS#12 files
- Add `pkcs12_pbmac1_pbkdf2_key_gen()` for use during PKCS#12 generation with PBMAC1

The implementation correctly rejects malformed PKCS#12 input that specifies an out-of-range key length or a non-OCTET-STRING salt type, preventing undefined behavior when processing untrusted files.
pr_title: Implementation of RFC 9579, PBMAC1 in PKCS#12 with input validation
release_caveats: Eligibility uses recorded canonical mainline fix alias; preserve construction fix and canonical fix separately. Independently checked ancestry/date and mapping evidence.

findings.message: The PBMAC1_PBKDF2_HMAC function reads PBKDF2 parameters from untrusted PKCS#12 input without validation. The keylength parameter is used directly without checking its bounds, and the salt parameter is accessed as an OCTET STRING without verifying its ASN.1 type. When keylength exceeds EVP_MAX_MD_SIZE (64 bytes), PKCS5_PBKDF2_HMAC will overflow the fixed-size stack buffer 'key[EVP_MAX_MD_SIZE]' defined in pkcs12_gen_mac. Additionally, if salt is not an OCTET STRING type, accessing pbkdf2_param->salt->value.octet_string leads to NULL or invalid pointer dereference. An attacker can craft a malicious PKCS#12 file with an oversized keylength value to achieve stack buffer overflow with attacker-controlled length, potentially enabling code execution.

related_locations.description: Fixed-size stack buffer declaration: unsigned char key[EVP_MAX_MD_SIZE]
PKCS5_PBKDF2_HMAC call that overflows the key buffer with unvalidated keylen

findings.suggestion: Validate the keylength parameter is present and within acceptable bounds (0 < keylen <= EVP_MAX_MD_SIZE) before using it. Also validate that salt is an OCTET STRING type before accessing its value.
findings.title: Stack buffer overflow via unvalidated PBKDF2 keylength in PBMAC1

ground_truth.root_cause: The PBMAC1 implementation in PKCS#12 support trusted ASN.1 parameters from untrusted input files without validation. The PBMAC1_PBKDF2_HMAC function extracts keylength and salt values from parsed PBKDF2PARAM structure and uses them directly without checking: (1) that keylength exists and is within valid bounds, and (2) that salt has the expected OCTET STRING ASN.1 type.

pr_description:
Reviewed-by: Paul Dale <ppzgs1@gmail.com>
Reviewed-by: Tomas Mraz <tomas@openssl.org>
(Merged from https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/24577)
pr_title: Implementation of the RFC 9579, PBMAC1 in PKCS#12
release_caveats: Eligibility uses recorded canonical mainline fix alias; preserve construction fix and canonical fix separately. Independently checked ancestry/date and mapping evidence.

agent_reasoning: The original (buggy) implementation used a two-step approach: first calling asn1_type_get_octetstring_int() with NULL to probe the IV length, checking only that i > 0, then calling it again with the stack buffer using the unchecked length i as the copy size. This meant an attacker-controlled IV longer than EVP_MAX_IV_LENGTH (16 bytes) in a crafted CMS AuthEnvelopedData message would overflow the stack buffer iv[EVP_MAX_IV_LENGTH]. The fix consolidates to a single call that passes the actual buffer and its capacity EVP_MAX_IV_LENGTH, then checks both i <= 0 and i > EVP_MAX_IV_LENGTH before proceeding. This ensures the length returned by ASN.1 parsing is within bounds before any data is used, preventing the stack buffer overflow.

intro_commit_message:
Add CMS AuthEnvelopedData with AES-GCM support

Add the AuthEnvelopedData as defined in RFC 5083 with AES-GCM
parameter as defined in RFC 5084.

Reviewed-by: Shane Lontis <shane.lontis@oracle.com>
Reviewed-by: Tomas Mraz <tmraz@fedoraproject.org>
(Merged from https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/8024)
pr_description:
This PR adds support for AuthEnvelopedData as defined in RFC 5083, using AES-GCM parameters as defined in RFC 5084.

The `evp_cipher_get_asn1_aead_params()` function extracts AEAD IV parameters from ASN.1-encoded CMS data. The implementation reads the IV directly into the fixed-size stack buffer `iv[EVP_MAX_IV_LENGTH]` in a single call to `asn1_type_get_octetstring_int()`, passing the buffer and its maximum capacity. The returned length is validated to be both positive and within the buffer size (`i <= 0 || i > EVP_MAX_IV_LENGTH`) before the IV is used, ensuring the buffer cannot be overflowed.

This approach is safer than a two-step length-probe-then-copy pattern: the data is read once with an explicit capacity bound, and the length check accounts for both underflow and overflow conditions before the IV is copied into the AEAD parameters structure.

findings.message: The function evp_cipher_get_asn1_aead_params() copies an IV (Initialization Vector) from ASN.1 encoded parameters into a fixed-size stack buffer without verifying that the IV length fits within the buffer. The code first calls asn1_type_get_octetstring_int() with NULL to get the length 'i' of the IV in the ASN.1 data, then only checks if 'i <= 0'. It does not check if 'i > EVP_MAX_IV_LENGTH'. The second call then copies 'i' bytes into the stack buffer 'iv[EVP_MAX_IV_LENGTH]', causing a stack-based buffer overflow if the attacker provides an oversized IV in a crafted CMS message. This overflow occurs before any authentication or tag verification, meaning no valid key material is required to trigger it.
findings.suggestion: Add a bounds check to verify that the IV length does not exceed EVP_MAX_IV_LENGTH before copying the data. Alternatively, combine both calls into a single call that copies directly to the buffer with proper size limits, and verify the returned length does not exceed the buffer size.
findings.title: Stack buffer overflow when parsing AEAD cipher IV from ASN.1

fix_commit.author: Igor Ustinov
fix_commit.message: Correct handling of AEAD-encrypted CMS with inadmissibly long IV

must_cover.reason: Primary location of finding: Stack buffer overflow when parsing AEAD cipher IV from ASN.1
Related location for: Stack buffer overflow when parsing AEAD cipher IV from ASN.1

ground_truth.root_cause: The evp_cipher_get_asn1_aead_params() function uses a two-step process to extract the IV: first calling asn1_type_get_octetstring_int() with NULL to obtain the length, then calling it again to copy the data. However, the bounds check between these calls only verifies the length is positive (i <= 0), not that it fits within the EVP_MAX_IV_LENGTH-sized stack buffer. The second call then uses the unchecked length 'i' as the buffer size parameter, allowing an attacker-controlled length to overflow the stack buffer.

agent_reasoning: Merged diff composed mechanically by cherry-picking fix b25396394002 on top of intro 547ea5882164 via git's 3-way merge. Vulnerability (NullPointerDereference): The function ossl_quic_get_cipher_by_char() calls ssl3_get_cipher_by_char(p) which can return NULL when the cipher ID is unknown or unsupported. The return value is stored in 'ciph' and immediately dereferenced on the next line (ciph->algorithm2) without checking if it is NULL. When a QUIC protocol client or server receives an unknown cipher suite from the peer, this results in a NULL pointer dereference, causing the process to crash with a Denial of Service. Root cause: The ossl_quic_get_cipher_by_char() function was added to support SSL_CIPHER_find() in QUIC connections but was implemented without proper NULL checking. The function assumes ssl3_get_cipher_by_char() will always return a valid pointer, but it returns NULL for unknown cipher IDs. This is a missing input validation bug where the return value of an external function call is not validated before use.

findings.message: The function ossl_quic_get_cipher_by_char() calls ssl3_get_cipher_by_char(p) which can return NULL when the cipher ID is unknown or unsupported. The return value is stored in 'ciph' and immediately dereferenced on the next line (ciph->algorithm2) without checking if it is NULL. When a QUIC protocol client or server receives an unknown cipher suite from the peer, this results in a NULL pointer dereference, causing the process to crash with a Denial of Service.
findings.suggestion: Add a NULL check for the return value of ssl3_get_cipher_by_char() before dereferencing the pointer. Return NULL early if the cipher is not found.
findings.title: NULL pointer dereference in ossl_quic_get_cipher_by_char()

Related location for: NULL pointer dereference in ossl_quic_get_cipher_by_char()

ground_truth.root_cause: The ossl_quic_get_cipher_by_char() function was added to support SSL_CIPHER_find() in QUIC connections but was implemented without proper NULL checking. The function assumes ssl3_get_cipher_by_char() will always return a valid pointer, but it returns NULL for unknown cipher IDs. This is a missing input validation bug where the return value of an external function call is not validated before use.

Reviewed-by: Hugo Landau <hlandau@openssl.org>

pr_title: Fix the SSL_CIPHER_find() function when used with a QCSO
release_caveats: Eligibility uses recorded canonical mainline fix alias; preserve construction fix and canonical fix separately. Independently checked ancestry/date and mapping evidence.

agent_reasoning:
The vulnerability was a silent truncation bug in `bio_to_mem()`. With `int maxlen` and a return value of "bytes read", when input exceeded the 16 MB limit the function would stop reading and return 16777216 — a positive number. The caller in `do_fp_oneshot_sign()` only checked `if (buflen <= 0)`, so truncation was indistinguishable from a full successful read. Any bytes beyond 16 MB were silently dropped, meaning a signature over a large file would only cover the first 16 MB; an attacker could modify content beyond that boundary without detection.

The fixed code changes `bio_to_mem()` to return a boolean success/failure indicator and pass the output length through a separate `size_t *` pointer. When `maxlen` is non-zero and the accumulated size exceeds it, the function immediately frees its buffer and returns `0` (error). The callers check `if (!bio_to_mem(...))` and report an error, aborting the operation. This ensures that signing or verification never proceeds with a truncated input.

fix_commit_message:
Report truncation in oneshot `openssl dgst -sign`

Previously input was silently truncated at 16MB, now if the input is
longer than limit, an error is reported.

The bio_to_mem() apps helper function was changed to return 0 or 1,
and return the size of the result via an output size_t pointer.

Fixes  CVE-2025-15469

intro_commit_message:
dgst commandline support for one shot signing algorithms

Reviewed-by: Paul Dale <ppzgs1@gmail.com>
Reviewed-by: Tim Hudson <tjh@openssl.org>
(Merged from https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/26697)
pr_description:
This PR improves the `bio_to_mem()` helper function in `apps/lib/apps.c` and updates its callers to properly handle input that exceeds the configured size limit.

Previously, `bio_to_mem()` accepted an `int maxlen` parameter and returned the number of bytes read (or -1 on error). When the input exceeded `maxlen`, the function would silently stop reading and return the bytes buffered so far as a success value. Callers like `do_fp_oneshot_sign()` in `apps/dgst.c` only checked for `buflen <= 0` as an error condition, so truncation at exactly 16 MB appeared as a successful read.

**Changes:**

- `bio_to_mem()` signature is updated to `int bio_to_mem(unsigned char **out, size_t *outlen, size_t maxlen, BIO *in)`, returning `1` on success and `0` on error, with the output length returned via the new `size_t *outlen` pointer.
- When `maxlen` is non-zero and the input exceeds `maxlen` bytes, `bio_to_mem()` now returns `0` (error) instead of silently truncating.
- When `maxlen` is zero, there is no limit (effectively `SIZE_MAX`).
- The internal buffer size is increased from 1024 to 4096 bytes for better I/O throughput.
- Memory ownership is transferred cleanly using `BIO_set_close(BIO_NOCLOSE)` / `BUF_MEM_free()` to avoid copying.
- `apps/include/apps.h` declaration updated to match the new signature.
- `apps/dgst.c`: `do_fp_oneshot_sign()` updated to use the new API; on truncation an error is now reported and the operation aborted.
- `apps/pkeyutl.c`: `buf_inlen` and `siglen` promoted to `size_t`; all `bio_to_mem()` call sites updated; unnecessary casts removed from `EVP_PKEY_verify`, `EVP_DigestVerify`, `EVP_DigestVerifyFinal`, and `do_keyop` calls.
- `apps/lib/apps.c`: added `#include "internal/numbers.h"` for `SIZE_MAX`.
pr_title: Report truncation error in oneshot openssl dgst -sign for large inputs
release_caveats: Eligibility uses recorded canonical mainline fix alias; preserve construction fix and canonical fix separately. Independently checked ancestry/date and mapping evidence.

findings.message: The do_fp_oneshot_sign function uses bio_to_mem() with a 16MB limit to buffer input data for one-shot signing algorithms (Ed25519, Ed448, ML-DSA). When input exceeds 16MB, bio_to_mem() silently stops reading at the limit and returns success (the number of bytes read) instead of an error. The subsequent error check 'if (buflen <= 0)' never triggers because buflen is a positive value (16MB). This causes the signing/verification to proceed with only the first 16MB of the file, leaving trailing data unauthenticated. An attacker could modify bytes beyond the 16MB boundary without detection if both signing and verification use the affected 'openssl dgst' command.
findings.suggestion: Modify bio_to_mem() to return an error when input exceeds maxlen, or change its return value semantics to separately indicate truncation. The fix changes bio_to_mem() to return 0/1 (failure/success) and pass the output size via a pointer parameter, returning an error if input is longer than maxlen.
findings.title: Silent truncation of input data beyond 16MB limit in one-shot signing

fix_commit.author: Viktor Dukhovni
fix_commit.message: Report truncation in oneshot `openssl dgst -sign`

must_cover.reason: Primary location of finding: Silent truncation of input data beyond 16MB limit in one-shot signing
Related location for: Silent truncation of input data beyond 16MB limit in one-shot signing

ground_truth.root_cause: The bio_to_mem() function in apps/lib/apps.c was designed to read a BIO into memory with an optional size limit. When the limit is reached (maxlen decrements to 0), the function breaks out of the read loop and returns the number of bytes successfully read as a success indicator. The calling code in do_fp_oneshot_sign() only checks for buflen <= 0 as an error condition, so truncation at exactly 16MB appears as a successful operation. The documentation stated that an error would be reported for overlarge inputs, but the implementation did not match this behavior.

agent_reasoning: The bug was a copy-paste error in the OPT_ADDREJECT handler: `sk_ASN1_OBJECT_push(trust, objtmp)` was used instead of `sk_ASN1_OBJECT_push(reject, objtmp)`. As a result, calling `openssl x509 -addreject <oid>` would silently add the object to the trust list rather than the reject list, completely inverting the intended security policy — a certificate would be treated as trusted for a use the user explicitly wanted to forbid. The fix changes the push target to `reject`, so the object is correctly recorded as a rejection and the downstream X509_TRUST machinery enforces the intended denial of trust.

agent_reasoning: The vulnerability arises because the stream (hardware-accelerated) path in both CRYPTO_ocb128_encrypt and CRYPTO_ocb128_decrypt processes all full blocks without advancing the `in`/`out` pointers. The tail-handling code that follows assumes the pointers already point past the full blocks (as they do after the scalar loop). When a message has trailing bytes and the stream path is taken, tail handling silently reprocesses the beginning of the buffer, leaving the real trailing bytes unencrypted and unauthenticated. The fix adds `processed_bytes = num_blocks * 16; in += processed_bytes; out += processed_bytes;` immediately after each `ctx->stream(...)` call, ensuring the pointers are correctly positioned before tail handling begins. This eliminates the plaintext-exposure and authentication-bypass on partial final blocks.

Fix OCB AES-NI/HW stream path unauthenticated/unencrypted trailing bytes

When ctx->stream (e.g., AES‑NI or ARMv8 CE) is available, the fast path

tail-handling code then operates on the base pointers, effectively reprocessing

pr_description:
When the hardware-accelerated stream path (`ctx->stream`, e.g. AES-NI or ARMv8 CE) is available in `CRYPTO_ocb128_encrypt` and `CRYPTO_ocb128_decrypt`, the fast path processes all full 16-byte blocks in one call. However, the `in` and `out` pointers were not advanced after the stream call, so any subsequent tail handling (for the remaining 1–15 bytes) would operate on the start of the buffer rather than the actual trailing bytes.

This change tracks the number of bytes processed by the stream path in a new local variable `processed_bytes`, then advances `in` and `out` by that amount before falling through to the tail-handling code. The scalar block-by-block path already advances `in` and `out` inside its loop, so it is unaffected.

Without this fix, messages whose length is not a multiple of 16 bytes and that use an AES-NI/HW-accelerated code path would have their trailing bytes left unencrypted (encryption) or decrypted from the wrong source (decryption), and the authentication checksum would not cover the true tail bytes.
pr_title: Fix OCB stream path failing to advance in/out pointers after block processing

findings.message: When the hardware-accelerated stream path (ctx->stream) is used in CRYPTO_ocb128_encrypt and CRYPTO_ocb128_decrypt, the code processes full 16-byte blocks but fails to advance the 'in' and 'out' pointers afterward. A refactor in this commit changed the tail-handling code to use bare 'in' and 'out' pointers (assuming they were advanced during block processing), but the stream path branch does not advance them. This causes the tail-handling code to operate on the beginning of the buffer instead of the actual trailing bytes (1-15 bytes). As a result, the trailing bytes are left unencrypted and unauthenticated, exposing plaintext and allowing undetected tampering.

Related location for: Missing pointer advancement in OCB hardware-accelerated stream path
Related location for: Missing pointer advancement in OCB hardware-accelerated stream path

ground_truth.root_cause: A refactoring commit (14bb100b) changed the OCB encrypt/decrypt functions to advance 'in' and 'out' pointers during block-by-block processing in the non-stream path, and changed the tail-handling code to use these pre-advanced pointers. However, the hardware-accelerated stream path (ctx->stream) processes blocks without advancing the pointers, creating an inconsistency. When trailing bytes exist and the stream path is taken, the tail-handling code operates on the original pointer positions (the beginning of the buffer) instead of the actual tail, leaving the real trailing bytes unprocessed.

agent_reasoning: Without these checks, a malformed or edge-case UTF-16/BMP input could cause UTF8_putc() to return -1. In OPENSSL_uni2utf8(), that -1 was added directly to asclen, making it negative, and the subsequent write of the NUL terminator at asctmp[asclen] would land before the allocated buffer — a heap corruption write. In do_buf(), a negative utflen would silently suppress characters without signaling an error upward. Both fixes ensure that a negative return from UTF8_putc (via bmp_to_utf8 or directly) is caught and propagated immediately, preventing any heap-corrupting arithmetic on the length accumulator.

intro_commit_message:
crypto/pkcs12: add UTF8 support.

Reviewed-by: Richard Levitte <levitte@openssl.org>
pr_description:
The UTF8_putc() function can return a negative value when it encounters an error (e.g., the output buffer is too small for the encoded character). Two call sites failed to check for this condition:

1. `crypto/asn1/a_strex.c` (`do_buf`): The `utflen` variable was assigned from `UTF8_putc()` without checking for a negative return. A negative value would cause the subsequent `for` loop to be skipped silently, but the underlying error was never propagated. This change combines the declaration and assignment into a single statement and adds an early return of -1 when `UTF8_putc` fails.

2. `crypto/pkcs12/p12_utl.c` (`OPENSSL_uni2utf8`): The second pass of the BMP-to-UTF-8 conversion loop called `bmp_to_utf8()` (which internally calls `UTF8_putc()`) without checking for a negative return value. A negative `j` would corrupt `asclen`, leading to an out-of-bounds write when the NUL terminator was placed at `asctmp[asclen]`. This change adds an explicit check: if `bmp_to_utf8()` returns a negative value, the allocated buffer is freed and NULL is returned to the caller.

findings.message: The OPENSSL_uni2utf8() function's second pass loop calls bmp_to_utf8() to emit UTF-8 characters but fails to check for a negative return value. The bmp_to_utf8() function passes the remaining UTF-16 source byte count (len) to UTF8_putc() as the destination buffer capacity. For BMP code points above U+07FF (requiring 3 UTF-8 bytes), if only 2 UTF-16 source bytes remain, UTF8_putc() returns -1 due to insufficient capacity. This -1 is then added to asclen without validation, making asclen negative. The subsequent NUL terminator write at asctmp[asclen] writes before the allocated buffer, causing heap corruption.

related_locations.description: Root cause: passes remaining UTF-16 byte count as destination capacity to UTF8_putc()
Write location: NUL terminator written at negative offset

findings.suggestion: Check the return value of bmp_to_utf8() in the second loop. If it returns a negative value, free the allocated buffer and return NULL to prevent heap corruption.
findings.title: Missing return value check in UTF-16 to UTF-8 conversion leads to negative index write

ground_truth.root_cause: The bmp_to_utf8() function misuses the 'len' parameter (remaining UTF-16 source bytes) as the destination buffer capacity argument to UTF8_putc(). This semantic mismatch causes UTF8_putc() to return -1 for valid BMP characters that require more UTF-8 bytes than the remaining source bytes. The calling function OPENSSL_uni2utf8() checks for negative returns in the first (sizing) pass but fails to do so in the second (writing) pass.

agent_reasoning: The bug-introducing commit added `ESS_SIGNING_CERT_get()` and `ESS_SIGNING_CERT_V2_get()` in `crypto/ess/ess_lib.c`. Both functions retrieve an `ASN1_TYPE` attribute from the PKCS7 signer info and immediately access `attr->value.sequence` without first verifying that `attr->type == V_ASN1_SEQUENCE`. Because `ASN1_TYPE.value` is a tagged union, accessing `.sequence` when the type field holds a different tag causes type confusion — the code interprets arbitrary bytes as an `ASN1_STRING*`, leading to NULL/invalid pointer dereference and denial of service when processing a malformed TimeStamp Response. The fix adds `|| attr->type != V_ASN1_SEQUENCE` to the null-check guard in both functions so that any attribute with an unexpected type is safely rejected before the union member is accessed.
commit_message:
[Merged] crypto/cms: Add support for CAdES Basic Electronic Signatures (CAdES-BES)

A CAdES Basic Electronic Signature (CAdES-BES) contains, among other
specifications, a collection of  Signing Certificate reference attributes,
stored in the signedData ether as ESS signing-certificate or as
ESS signing-certificate-v2. These are described in detail in Section 5.7.2
of RFC 5126 - CMS Advanced Electronic Signatures (CAdES).

This patch adds support for adding  ESS signing-certificate[-v2] attributes
to CMS signedData. Although it implements only a small part of the RFC, it
is sufficient many cases to enable the `openssl cms` app to create signatures
which comply with legal requirements of some European States (e.g Italy).

+=head1 CAdES Basic Electronic Signature (CAdES-BES)
+
+A CAdES Basic Electronic Signature (CAdES-BES), as defined in the European Standard ETSI EN 319 122-1 V1.1.1, contains:
+
+=over 4
+
+=item *
+
+The signed user data as defined in CMS (RFC 3852);
+
+=item *
+
+Content-type of the EncapsulatedContentInfo value being signed;
+
+=item *
+
+Message-digest of the eContent OCTET STRING within encapContentInfo being signed;
+
+=item *
+
+An ESS signing-certificate or ESS signing-certificate-v2 attribute, as defined in Enhanced Security Services (ESS), RFC 2634 and RFC 5035.
+An ESS signing-certificate attribute only allows for the use of SHA-1 as a digest algorithm.
+An ESS signing-certificate-v2 attribute allows for the use of any digest algorithm.
+
+=item *
+
+The digital signature value computed on the user data and, when present, on the signed attributes.
+
+Note that currently the B<-cades> option applies only to the B<-sign> operation and is ignored during
+the B<-verify> operation, i.e. the signing certification is not checked during the verification process.

+

diff --git a/doc/man3/CMS_add1_signing_cert.pod b/doc/man3/CMS_add1_signing_cert.pod
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..035e679d2c
--- /dev/null
+++ b/doc/man3/CMS_add1_signing_cert.pod
@@ -0,0 +1,45 @@
+=pod
+
+=head1 NAME
+
+CMS_add1_signing_cert, CMS_add1_signing_cert_v2
+- add ESS signing-certificate signed attribute to a
+CMS_SignerInfo data structure
+
+=head1 SYNOPSIS
+
+ #include <openssl/cms.h>
+
+ int CMS_add1_signing_cert(CMS_SignerInfo *si, ESS_SIGNING_CERT *sc);
+
+ int CMS_add1_signing_cert_v2(CMS_SignerInfo *si, ESS_SIGNING_CERT_V2 *sc2);
+
+=head1 DESCRIPTION
+
+CMS_add1_signing_cert() adds an ESS Signing Certificate B<sc> (version 1) signed
+attribute to the CMS_SignerInfo B<si>.
+CMS_add1_signing_cert_v2() adds an ESS Signing Certificate B<sc2> (version 2) signed
+attribute to the CMS_SignerInfo B<si>.
+The ESS Signing Certificate attributes version 1 and 2 are defined in RFC 5035
+which updates Section 5.4 of RFC 2634.
+
+=head1 NOTES
+
+This attribute is mandatory to make a CMS compliant with CAdES-BES
+(European Standard ETSI EN 319 122-1 V1.1.1).
+For a fuller description see L<cms(1)>).
+

fix_commit_message:
Verify ASN1 object's types before attempting to access them as a particular type

Issue was reported in ossl_ess_get_signing_cert but is also present in
ossl_ess_get_signing_cert_v2.

Fixes: https://github.com/openssl/srt/issues/61
Fixes CVE-2025-69420

Reviewed-by: Norbert Pocs <norbertp@openssl.org>
Reviewed-by: Saša Nedvědický <sashan@openssl.org>
Reviewed-by: Tomas Mraz <tomas@openssl.org>
MergeDate: Mon Jan 26 19:53:36 2026
(cherry picked from commit ea8fc4c345fbd749048809c9f7c881ea656b0b94)

@@ -0,0 +1,269 @@
+/*

+
+#include <string.h>
+#include <openssl/x509v3.h>
+#include <openssl/err.h>
+#include <openssl/ess.h>
+#include "internal/ess_int.h"
+
+static ESS_CERT_ID *ESS_CERT_ID_new_init(X509 *cert, int issuer_needed);
+static ESS_CERT_ID_V2 *ESS_CERT_ID_V2_new_init(const EVP_MD *hash_alg,
+                                               X509 *cert, int issuer_needed);
+
+ESS_SIGNING_CERT *ESS_SIGNING_CERT_new_init(X509 *signcert,
+                                            STACK_OF(X509) *certs,
+                                            int issuer_needed)
+{
+    ESS_CERT_ID *cid = NULL;
+    ESS_SIGNING_CERT *sc;
+    int i;
+
+    if ((sc = ESS_SIGNING_CERT_new()) == NULL)
+        goto err;
+    if (sc->cert_ids == NULL
+        && (sc->cert_ids = sk_ESS_CERT_ID_new_null()) == NULL)
+        goto err;
+
+    if ((cid = ESS_CERT_ID_new_init(signcert, issuer_needed)) == NULL
+        || !sk_ESS_CERT_ID_push(sc->cert_ids, cid))
+        goto err;
+    for (i = 0; i < sk_X509_num(certs); ++i) {
+        X509 *cert = sk_X509_value(certs, i);
+        if ((cid = ESS_CERT_ID_new_init(cert, 1)) == NULL
+            || !sk_ESS_CERT_ID_push(sc->cert_ids, cid))
+            goto err;
+    }
+
+    return sc;
+ err:
+    ESS_SIGNING_CERT_free(sc);
+    ESS_CERT_ID_free(cid);
+    ESSerr(ESS_F_ESS_SIGNING_CERT_NEW_INIT, ERR_R_MALLOC_FAILURE);
+    return NULL;
+}
+
+static ESS_CERT_ID *ESS_CERT_ID_new_init(X509 *cert, int issuer_needed)
+{
+    ESS_CERT_ID *cid = NULL;
+    GENERAL_NAME *name = NULL;
+    unsigned char cert_sha1[SHA_DIGEST_LENGTH];
+
+    /* Call for side-effect of computing hash and caching extensions */
+    X509_check_purpose(cert, -1, 0);
+    if ((cid = ESS_CERT_ID_new()) == NULL)
+        goto err;
+    X509_digest(cert, EVP_sha1(), cert_sha1, NULL);
+    if (!ASN1_OCTET_STRING_set(cid->hash, cert_sha1, SHA_DIGEST_LENGTH))
+        goto err;
+
+    /* Setting the issuer/serial if requested. */
+    if (!issuer_needed)
+        return cid;
+
+    if (cid->issuer_serial == NULL
+        && (cid->issuer_serial = ESS_ISSUER_SERIAL_new()) == NULL)
+        goto err;
+    if ((name = GENERAL_NAME_new()) == NULL)
+        goto err;
+    name->type = GEN_DIRNAME;
+    if ((name->d.dirn = X509_NAME_dup(X509_get_issuer_name(cert))) == NULL)
+        goto err;
+    if (!sk_GENERAL_NAME_push(cid->issuer_serial->issuer, name))
+        goto err;
+    name = NULL;            /* Ownership is lost. */
+    ASN1_INTEGER_free(cid->issuer_serial->serial);
+    if (!(cid->issuer_serial->serial =
+          ASN1_INTEGER_dup(X509_get_serialNumber(cert))))
+        goto err;
+
+    return cid;
+ err:
+    GENERAL_NAME_free(name);
+    ESS_CERT_ID_free(cid);
+    ESSerr(ESS_F_ESS_CERT_ID_NEW_INIT, ERR_R_MALLOC_FAILURE);
+    return NULL;
+}
+
+ESS_SIGNING_CERT_V2 *ESS_SIGNING_CERT_V2_new_init(const EVP_MD *hash_alg,
+                                                  X509 *signcert,
+                                                  STACK_OF(X509) *certs,
+                                                  int issuer_needed)
+{
+    ESS_CERT_ID_V2 *cid = NULL;
+    ESS_SIGNING_CERT_V2 *sc;
+    int i;
+
+    if ((sc = ESS_SIGNING_CERT_V2_new()) == NULL)
+        goto err;
+    if ((cid = ESS_CERT_ID_V2_new_init(hash_alg, signcert, issuer_needed)) == NULL)
+        goto err;
+    if (!sk_ESS_CERT_ID_V2_push(sc->cert_ids, cid))
+        goto err;
+    cid = NULL;
+
+    for (i = 0; i < sk_X509_num(certs); ++i) {
+        X509 *cert = sk_X509_value(certs, i);
+
+        if ((cid = ESS_CERT_ID_V2_new_init(hash_alg, cert, 1)) == NULL)
+            goto err;
+        if (!sk_ESS_CERT_ID_V2_push(sc->cert_ids, cid))
+            goto err;
+        cid = NULL;
+    }
+
+    return sc;
+ err:
+    ESS_SIGNING_CERT_V2_free(sc);
+    ESS_CERT_ID_V2_free(cid);
+    ESSerr(ESS_F_ESS_SIGNING_CERT_V2_NEW_INIT, ERR_R_MALLOC_FAILURE);
+    return NULL;
+}
+
+static ESS_CERT_ID_V2 *ESS_CERT_ID_V2_new_init(const EVP_MD *hash_alg,
+                                               X509 *cert, int issuer_needed)
+{
+    ESS_CERT_ID_V2 *cid;
+    GENERAL_NAME *name = NULL;
+    unsigned char hash[EVP_MAX_MD_SIZE];
+    unsigned int hash_len = sizeof(hash);
+    X509_ALGOR *alg = NULL;
+
+    memset(hash, 0, sizeof(hash));
+
+    if ((cid = ESS_CERT_ID_V2_new()) == NULL)
+        goto err;
+
+    if (hash_alg != EVP_sha256()) {
+        alg = X509_ALGOR_new();
+        if (alg == NULL)
+            goto err;
+        X509_ALGOR_set_md(alg, hash_alg);
+        if (alg->algorithm == NULL)
+            goto err;
+        cid->hash_alg = alg;
+        alg = NULL;
+    } else {
+        cid->hash_alg = NULL;
+    }
+
+    if (!X509_digest(cert, hash_alg, hash, &hash_len))
+        goto err;
+
+    if (!ASN1_OCTET_STRING_set(cid->hash, hash, hash_len))
+        goto err;
+
+    if (!issuer_needed)
+        return cid;
+
+    if ((cid->issuer_serial = ESS_ISSUER_SERIAL_new()) == NULL)
+        goto err;
+    if ((name = GENERAL_NAME_new()) == NULL)
+        goto err;
+    name->type = GEN_DIRNAME;
+    if ((name->d.dirn = X509_NAME_dup(X509_get_issuer_name(cert))) == NULL)
+        goto err;
+    if (!sk_GENERAL_NAME_push(cid->issuer_serial->issuer, name))
+        goto err;
+    name = NULL;            /* Ownership is lost. */
+    ASN1_INTEGER_free(cid->issuer_serial->serial);
+    cid->issuer_serial->serial = ASN1_INTEGER_dup(X509_get_serialNumber(cert));
+    if (cid->issuer_serial->serial == NULL)
+        goto err;
+
+    return cid;
+ err:
+    X509_ALGOR_free(alg);
+    GENERAL_NAME_free(name);
+    ESS_CERT_ID_V2_free(cid);
+    ESSerr(ESS_F_ESS_CERT_ID_V2_NEW_INIT, ERR_R_MALLOC_FAILURE);
+    return NULL;
+}
+
+ESS_SIGNING_CERT *ESS_SIGNING_CERT_get(PKCS7_SIGNER_INFO *si)
+{
+    ASN1_TYPE *attr;
+    const unsigned char *p;
+    attr = PKCS7_get_signed_attribute(si, NID_id_smime_aa_signingCertificate);
+    if (!attr || attr->type != V_ASN1_SEQUENCE)
+        return NULL;
+    p = attr->value.sequence->data;
+    return d2i_ESS_SIGNING_CERT(NULL, &p, attr->value.sequence->length);
+}
+
+ESS_SIGNING_CERT_V2 *ESS_SIGNING_CERT_V2_get(PKCS7_SIGNER_INFO *si)
+{
+    ASN1_TYPE *attr;
+    const unsigned char *p;
+
+    attr = PKCS7_get_signed_attribute(si, NID_id_smime_aa_signingCertificateV2);
+    if (attr == NULL || attr->type != V_ASN1_SEQUENCE)
+        return NULL;
+    p = attr->value.sequence->data;
+    return d2i_ESS_SIGNING_CERT_V2(NULL, &p, attr->value.sequence->length);
+}
+
+int ESS_SIGNING_CERT_add(PKCS7_SIGNER_INFO *si, ESS_SIGNING_CERT *sc)
+{
+    ASN1_STRING *seq = NULL;
+    unsigned char *p, *pp = NULL;
+    int len;
+
+    len = i2d_ESS_SIGNING_CERT(sc, NULL);
+    if ((pp = OPENSSL_malloc(len)) == NULL) {
+        ESSerr(ESS_F_ESS_SIGNING_CERT_ADD, ERR_R_MALLOC_FAILURE);
+        goto err;
+    }
+    p = pp;
+    i2d_ESS_SIGNING_CERT(sc, &p);
+    if ((seq = ASN1_STRING_new()) == NULL || !ASN1_STRING_set(seq, pp, len)) {
+        ESSerr(ESS_F_ESS_SIGNING_CERT_ADD, ERR_R_MALLOC_FAILURE);
+        goto err;
+    }
+    OPENSSL_free(pp);
+    pp = NULL;
+    return PKCS7_add_signed_attribute(si,
+                                      NID_id_smime_aa_signingCertificate,
+                                      V_ASN1_SEQUENCE, seq);
+ err:
+    ASN1_STRING_free(seq);
+    OPENSSL_free(pp);
+
+    return 0;
+}
+
+int ESS_SIGNING_CERT_V2_add(PKCS7_SIGNER_INFO *si,
+                            ESS_SIGNING_CERT_V2 *sc)
+{
+    ASN1_STRING *seq = NULL;
+    unsigned char *p, *pp = NULL;
+    int len = i2d_ESS_SIGNING_CERT_V2(sc, NULL);
+
+    if ((pp = OPENSSL_malloc(len)) == NULL) {
+        ESSerr(ESS_F_ESS_SIGNING_CERT_V2_ADD, ERR_R_MALLOC_FAILURE);
+        goto err;
+    }
+
+    p = pp;
+    i2d_ESS_SIGNING_CERT_V2(sc, &p);
+    if ((seq = ASN1_STRING_new()) == NULL || !ASN1_STRING_set(seq, pp, len)) {
+        ESSerr(ESS_F_ESS_SIGNING_CERT_V2_ADD, ERR_R_MALLOC_FAILURE);
+        goto err;
+    }
+
+    OPENSSL_free(pp);
+    pp = NULL;
+    return PKCS7_add_signed_attribute(si,
+                                      NID_id_smime_aa_signingCertificateV2,
+                                      V_ASN1_SEQUENCE, seq);
+ err:
+    ASN1_STRING_free(seq);
+    OPENSSL_free(pp);
+    return 0;
+}

+    ESS_ISSUER_SERIAL *issuer_serial;

+ *        policies                SEQUENCE OF PolicyInformation OPTIONAL
+ * }
+ */
+
+struct ESS_signing_cert_v2_st {
+    STACK_OF(ESS_CERT_ID_V2) *cert_ids;
+    STACK_OF(POLICYINFO) *policy_info;
+};

+=head1 CAdES Basic Electronic Signature (CAdES-BES)
+
+A CAdES Basic Electronic Signature (CAdES-BES), as defined in the European Standard ETSI EN 319 122-1 V1.1.1, contains:
+
+=over 4
+
+=item *
+
+The signed user data as defined in CMS (RFC 3852);
+
+=item *
+
+Content-type of the EncapsulatedContentInfo value being signed;
+
+=item *
+
+Message-digest of the eContent OCTET STRING within encapContentInfo being signed;
+
+=item *
+
+An ESS signing-certificate or ESS signing-certificate-v2 attribute, as defined in Enhanced Security Services (ESS), RFC 2634 and RFC 5035.
+An ESS signing-certificate attribute only allows for the use of SHA-1 as a digest algorithm.
+An ESS signing-certificate-v2 attribute allows for the use of any digest algorithm.
+
+=item *
+
+The digital signature value computed on the user data and, when present, on the signed attributes.
+
+Note that currently the B<-cades> option applies only to the B<-sign> operation and is ignored during
+the B<-verify> operation, i.e. the signing certification is not checked during the verification process.
+This feature might be added in a future version.
+
+=back

@@ -0,0 +1,45 @@
+=pod
+
+=head1 NAME
+
+CMS_add1_signing_cert, CMS_add1_signing_cert_v2
+- add ESS signing-certificate signed attribute to a
+CMS_SignerInfo data structure
+
+=head1 SYNOPSIS
+
+ #include <openssl/cms.h>
+
+ int CMS_add1_signing_cert(CMS_SignerInfo *si, ESS_SIGNING_CERT *sc);
+
+ int CMS_add1_signing_cert_v2(CMS_SignerInfo *si, ESS_SIGNING_CERT_V2 *sc2);
+
+=head1 DESCRIPTION
+
+CMS_add1_signing_cert() adds an ESS Signing Certificate B<sc> (version 1) signed
+attribute to the CMS_SignerInfo B<si>.
+CMS_add1_signing_cert_v2() adds an ESS Signing Certificate B<sc2> (version 2) signed
+attribute to the CMS_SignerInfo B<si>.
+The ESS Signing Certificate attributes version 1 and 2 are defined in RFC 5035
+which updates Section 5.4 of RFC 2634.
+
+=head1 NOTES
+
+This attribute is mandatory to make a CMS compliant with CAdES-BES
+(European Standard ETSI EN 319 122-1 V1.1.1).
+For a fuller description see L<cms(1)>).
+
+=head1 RETURN VALUES
+
+CMS_add1_signing_cert() and CMS_add1_signing_cert_v2() return 1 if attribute is added or 0 if an error occurred.
+

intro_commit_message:
crypto/cms: Add support for CAdES Basic Electronic Signatures (CAdES-BES)

A CAdES Basic Electronic Signature (CAdES-BES) contains, among other
specifications, a collection of  Signing Certificate reference attributes,
stored in the signedData ether as ESS signing-certificate or as
ESS signing-certificate-v2. These are described in detail in Section 5.7.2
of RFC 5126 - CMS Advanced Electronic Signatures (CAdES).

This patch adds support for adding  ESS signing-certificate[-v2] attributes
to CMS signedData. Although it implements only a small part of the RFC, it
is sufficient many cases to enable the `openssl cms` app to create signatures
which comply with legal requirements of some European States (e.g Italy).

Reviewed-by: Richard Levitte <levitte@openssl.org>
Reviewed-by: Matthias St. Pierre <Matthias.St.Pierre@ncp-e.com>
(Merged from https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/7893)
pr_description:
This patch adds support for ESS signing-certificate and ESS signing-certificate-v2 attributes in CMS signedData, implementing a subset of RFC 5126 (CMS Advanced Electronic Signatures / CAdES).

CAdES-BES signatures contain Signing Certificate reference attributes that bind the signer's certificate to the signature. This prevents certificate substitution attacks by cryptographically referencing the specific certificate used for signing.

The implementation adds:
- `ESS_SIGNING_CERT_new_init()` and `ESS_SIGNING_CERT_V2_new_init()` to create signing certificate attribute structures
- `ESS_SIGNING_CERT_get()` and `ESS_SIGNING_CERT_V2_get()` to retrieve and decode these attributes from PKCS7 signer info, with proper ASN.1 type validation before accessing the sequence data
- `ESS_SIGNING_CERT_add()` and `ESS_SIGNING_CERT_V2_add()` to attach these attributes to a PKCS7 signer info structure

The getter functions validate that the retrieved ASN1_TYPE attribute carries the expected `V_ASN1_SEQUENCE` type before dereferencing the sequence member, preventing type confusion if a malformed input supplies an attribute with an unexpected type tag.

Although this implements only a small part of the RFC, it is sufficient in many cases to enable the `openssl cms` application to create signatures complying with the legal requirements of some European states (e.g. Italy).
pr_title: crypto/cms: Add support for CAdES Basic Electronic Signatures (CAdES-BES)

+=head1 CAdES Basic Electronic Signature (CAdES-BES)
+
+A CAdES Basic Electronic Signature (CAdES-BES), as defined in the European Standard ETSI EN 319 122-1 V1.1.1, contains:

+

diff --git a/doc/man3/CMS_add1_signing_cert.pod b/doc/man3/CMS_add1_signing_cert.pod
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..035e679d2c
--- /dev/null
+++ b/doc/man3/CMS_add1_signing_cert.pod
@@ -0,0 +1,45 @@
+=pod
+
+=head1 NAME
+
+CMS_add1_signing_cert, CMS_add1_signing_cert_v2
+- add ESS signing-certificate signed attribute to a
+CMS_SignerInfo data structure
+
+=head1 SYNOPSIS
+
+ #include <openssl/cms.h>
+
+ int CMS_add1_signing_cert(CMS_SignerInfo *si, ESS_SIGNING_CERT *sc);
+
+ int CMS_add1_signing_cert_v2(CMS_SignerInfo *si, ESS_SIGNING_CERT_V2 *sc2);
+
+=head1 DESCRIPTION
+
+CMS_add1_signing_cert() adds an ESS Signing Certificate B<sc> (version 1) signed
+attribute to the CMS_SignerInfo B<si>.
+CMS_add1_signing_cert_v2() adds an ESS Signing Certificate B<sc2> (version 2) signed
+attribute to the CMS_SignerInfo B<si>.
+The ESS Signing Certificate attributes version 1 and 2 are defined in RFC 5035
+which updates Section 5.4 of RFC 2634.
+
+=head1 NOTES
+
+This attribute is mandatory to make a CMS compliant with CAdES-BES
+(European Standard ETSI EN 319 122-1 V1.1.1).
+For a fuller description see L<cms(1)>).
+
+=head1 RETURN VALUES
+
+CMS_add1_signing_cert() and CMS_add1_signing_cert_v2() return 1 if attribute is added or 0 if an error occurred.
+

+ * Add signer certificate's V2 digest to a SignerInfo
+ * structure
+ */
+
+int CMS_add1_signing_cert_v2(CMS_SignerInfo *si,
+                             ESS_SIGNING_CERT_V2 *sc)
+{
+    ASN1_STRING *seq = NULL;
+    unsigned char *p, *pp;
+    int len;
+
+    /* Add SigningCertificateV2 signed attribute to the signer info. */
+    len = i2d_ESS_SIGNING_CERT_V2(sc, NULL);
+    if ((pp = OPENSSL_malloc(len)) == NULL)
+        goto err;
+    p = pp;
+    i2d_ESS_SIGNING_CERT_V2(sc, &p);
+    if (!(seq = ASN1_STRING_new()) || !ASN1_STRING_set(seq, pp, len))
+        goto err;
+    OPENSSL_free(pp);
+    pp = NULL;
+    if (!CMS_signed_add1_attr_by_NID(si, NID_id_smime_aa_signingCertificateV2,
+                                     V_ASN1_SEQUENCE, seq, -1))
+        goto err;
+    ASN1_STRING_free(seq);
+    return 1;
+ err:
+    CMSerr(CMS_F_CMS_ADD1_SIGNING_CERT_V2, ERR_R_MALLOC_FAILURE);
+    ASN1_STRING_free(seq);
+    OPENSSL_free(pp);
+    return 0;

+        goto err;
+    OPENSSL_free(pp);
+    pp = NULL;
+    if (!CMS_signed_add1_attr_by_NID(si, NID_id_smime_aa_signingCertificate,
+                                     V_ASN1_SEQUENCE, seq, -1))
+        goto err;
+    ASN1_STRING_free(seq);
+    return 1;
+ err:
+    CMSerr(CMS_F_CMS_ADD1_SIGNING_CERT, ERR_R_MALLOC_FAILURE);
+    ASN1_STRING_free(seq);
+    OPENSSL_free(pp);
+    return 0;

index 0000000000..fa9cff18be
--- /dev/null
+++ b/crypto/ess/ess_lib.c
@@ -0,0 +1,269 @@
+/*

+ *
+ * Licensed under the Apache License 2.0 (the "License").  You may not use
+ * this file except in compliance with the License.  You can obtain a copy

+
+#include <string.h>
+#include <openssl/x509v3.h>
+#include <openssl/err.h>
+#include <openssl/ess.h>
+#include "internal/ess_int.h"
+
+static ESS_CERT_ID *ESS_CERT_ID_new_init(X509 *cert, int issuer_needed);
+static ESS_CERT_ID_V2 *ESS_CERT_ID_V2_new_init(const EVP_MD *hash_alg,
+                                               X509 *cert, int issuer_needed);
+
+ESS_SIGNING_CERT *ESS_SIGNING_CERT_new_init(X509 *signcert,
+                                            STACK_OF(X509) *certs,
+                                            int issuer_needed)
+{
+    ESS_CERT_ID *cid = NULL;
+    ESS_SIGNING_CERT *sc;
+    int i;
+
+    if ((sc = ESS_SIGNING_CERT_new()) == NULL)
+        goto err;
+    if (sc->cert_ids == NULL
+        && (sc->cert_ids = sk_ESS_CERT_ID_new_null()) == NULL)
+        goto err;
+
+    if ((cid = ESS_CERT_ID_new_init(signcert, issuer_needed)) == NULL
+        || !sk_ESS_CERT_ID_push(sc->cert_ids, cid))
+        goto err;
+    for (i = 0; i < sk_X509_num(certs); ++i) {
+        X509 *cert = sk_X509_value(certs, i);
+        if ((cid = ESS_CERT_ID_new_init(cert, 1)) == NULL
+            || !sk_ESS_CERT_ID_push(sc->cert_ids, cid))
+            goto err;
+    }
+
+    return sc;
+ err:
+    ESS_SIGNING_CERT_free(sc);
+    ESS_CERT_ID_free(cid);
+    ESSerr(ESS_F_ESS_SIGNING_CERT_NEW_INIT, ERR_R_MALLOC_FAILURE);
+    return NULL;
+}
+
+static ESS_CERT_ID *ESS_CERT_ID_new_init(X509 *cert, int issuer_needed)
+{
+    ESS_CERT_ID *cid = NULL;
+    GENERAL_NAME *name = NULL;
+    unsigned char cert_sha1[SHA_DIGEST_LENGTH];
+
+    /* Call for side-effect of computing hash and caching extensions */
+    X509_check_purpose(cert, -1, 0);
+    if ((cid = ESS_CERT_ID_new()) == NULL)
+        goto err;
+    X509_digest(cert, EVP_sha1(), cert_sha1, NULL);
+    if (!ASN1_OCTET_STRING_set(cid->hash, cert_sha1, SHA_DIGEST_LENGTH))
+        goto err;
+
+    /* Setting the issuer/serial if requested. */
+    if (!issuer_needed)
+        return cid;
+
+    if (cid->issuer_serial == NULL
+        && (cid->issuer_serial = ESS_ISSUER_SERIAL_new()) == NULL)
+        goto err;
+    if ((name = GENERAL_NAME_new()) == NULL)
+        goto err;
+    name->type = GEN_DIRNAME;
+    if ((name->d.dirn = X509_NAME_dup(X509_get_issuer_name(cert))) == NULL)
+        goto err;
+    if (!sk_GENERAL_NAME_push(cid->issuer_serial->issuer, name))
+        goto err;
+    name = NULL;            /* Ownership is lost. */
+    ASN1_INTEGER_free(cid->issuer_serial->serial);
+    if (!(cid->issuer_serial->serial =
+          ASN1_INTEGER_dup(X509_get_serialNumber(cert))))
+        goto err;
+
+    return cid;
+ err:
+    GENERAL_NAME_free(name);
+    ESS_CERT_ID_free(cid);
+    ESSerr(ESS_F_ESS_CERT_ID_NEW_INIT, ERR_R_MALLOC_FAILURE);
+    return NULL;
+}
+
+ESS_SIGNING_CERT_V2 *ESS_SIGNING_CERT_V2_new_init(const EVP_MD *hash_alg,
+                                                  X509 *signcert,
+                                                  STACK_OF(X509) *certs,
+                                                  int issuer_needed)
+{
+    ESS_CERT_ID_V2 *cid = NULL;
+    ESS_SIGNING_CERT_V2 *sc;
+    int i;
+
+    if ((sc = ESS_SIGNING_CERT_V2_new()) == NULL)
+        goto err;
+    if ((cid = ESS_CERT_ID_V2_new_init(hash_alg, signcert, issuer_needed)) == NULL)
+        goto err;
+    if (!sk_ESS_CERT_ID_V2_push(sc->cert_ids, cid))
+        goto err;
+    cid = NULL;
+
+    for (i = 0; i < sk_X509_num(certs); ++i) {
+        X509 *cert = sk_X509_value(certs, i);
+
+        if ((cid = ESS_CERT_ID_V2_new_init(hash_alg, cert, 1)) == NULL)
+            goto err;
+        if (!sk_ESS_CERT_ID_V2_push(sc->cert_ids, cid))
+            goto err;
+        cid = NULL;
+    }
+
+    return sc;
+ err:
+    ESS_SIGNING_CERT_V2_free(sc);
+    ESS_CERT_ID_V2_free(cid);
+    ESSerr(ESS_F_ESS_SIGNING_CERT_V2_NEW_INIT, ERR_R_MALLOC_FAILURE);
+    return NULL;
+}
+
+static ESS_CERT_ID_V2 *ESS_CERT_ID_V2_new_init(const EVP_MD *hash_alg,
+                                               X509 *cert, int issuer_needed)
+{
+    ESS_CERT_ID_V2 *cid;
+    GENERAL_NAME *name = NULL;
+    unsigned char hash[EVP_MAX_MD_SIZE];
+    unsigned int hash_len = sizeof(hash);
+    X509_ALGOR *alg = NULL;
+
+    memset(hash, 0, sizeof(hash));
+
+    if ((cid = ESS_CERT_ID_V2_new()) == NULL)
+        goto err;
+
+    if (hash_alg != EVP_sha256()) {
+        alg = X509_ALGOR_new();
+        if (alg == NULL)
+            goto err;
+        X509_ALGOR_set_md(alg, hash_alg);
+        if (alg->algorithm == NULL)
+            goto err;
+        cid->hash_alg = alg;
+        alg = NULL;
+    } else {
+        cid->hash_alg = NULL;
+    }
+
+    if (!X509_digest(cert, hash_alg, hash, &hash_len))
+        goto err;
+
+    if (!ASN1_OCTET_STRING_set(cid->hash, hash, hash_len))
+        goto err;
+
+    if (!issuer_needed)
+        return cid;
+
+    if ((cid->issuer_serial = ESS_ISSUER_SERIAL_new()) == NULL)
+        goto err;
+    if ((name = GENERAL_NAME_new()) == NULL)
+        goto err;
+    name->type = GEN_DIRNAME;
+    if ((name->d.dirn = X509_NAME_dup(X509_get_issuer_name(cert))) == NULL)
+        goto err;
+    if (!sk_GENERAL_NAME_push(cid->issuer_serial->issuer, name))
+        goto err;
+    name = NULL;            /* Ownership is lost. */
+    ASN1_INTEGER_free(cid->issuer_serial->serial);
+    cid->issuer_serial->serial = ASN1_INTEGER_dup(X509_get_serialNumber(cert));
+    if (cid->issuer_serial->serial == NULL)
+        goto err;
+
+    return cid;
+ err:
+    X509_ALGOR_free(alg);
+    GENERAL_NAME_free(name);
+    ESS_CERT_ID_V2_free(cid);
+    ESSerr(ESS_F_ESS_CERT_ID_V2_NEW_INIT, ERR_R_MALLOC_FAILURE);
+    return NULL;
+}
+
+ESS_SIGNING_CERT *ESS_SIGNING_CERT_get(PKCS7_SIGNER_INFO *si)
+{
+    ASN1_TYPE *attr;
+    const unsigned char *p;
+    attr = PKCS7_get_signed_attribute(si, NID_id_smime_aa_signingCertificate);
+    if (!attr)
+        return NULL;
+    p = attr->value.sequence->data;
+    return d2i_ESS_SIGNING_CERT(NULL, &p, attr->value.sequence->length);
+}
+
+ESS_SIGNING_CERT_V2 *ESS_SIGNING_CERT_V2_get(PKCS7_SIGNER_INFO *si)
+{
+    ASN1_TYPE *attr;
+    const unsigned char *p;
+
+    attr = PKCS7_get_signed_attribute(si, NID_id_smime_aa_signingCertificateV2);
+    if (attr == NULL)
+        return NULL;
+    p = attr->value.sequence->data;
+    return d2i_ESS_SIGNING_CERT_V2(NULL, &p, attr->value.sequence->length);
+}
+
+int ESS_SIGNING_CERT_add(PKCS7_SIGNER_INFO *si, ESS_SIGNING_CERT *sc)
+{
+    ASN1_STRING *seq = NULL;
+    unsigned char *p, *pp = NULL;
+    int len;
+
+    len = i2d_ESS_SIGNING_CERT(sc, NULL);
+    if ((pp = OPENSSL_malloc(len)) == NULL) {
+        ESSerr(ESS_F_ESS_SIGNING_CERT_ADD, ERR_R_MALLOC_FAILURE);
+        goto err;
+    }
+    p = pp;
+    i2d_ESS_SIGNING_CERT(sc, &p);
+    if ((seq = ASN1_STRING_new()) == NULL || !ASN1_STRING_set(seq, pp, len)) {
+        ESSerr(ESS_F_ESS_SIGNING_CERT_ADD, ERR_R_MALLOC_FAILURE);
+        goto err;
+    }
+    OPENSSL_free(pp);
+    pp = NULL;
+    return PKCS7_add_signed_attribute(si,
+                                      NID_id_smime_aa_signingCertificate,
+                                      V_ASN1_SEQUENCE, seq);
+ err:
+    ASN1_STRING_free(seq);
+    OPENSSL_free(pp);
+
+    return 0;
+}
+
+int ESS_SIGNING_CERT_V2_add(PKCS7_SIGNER_INFO *si,
+                            ESS_SIGNING_CERT_V2 *sc)
+{
+    ASN1_STRING *seq = NULL;
+    unsigned char *p, *pp = NULL;
+    int len = i2d_ESS_SIGNING_CERT_V2(sc, NULL);
+
+    if ((pp = OPENSSL_malloc(len)) == NULL) {
+        ESSerr(ESS_F_ESS_SIGNING_CERT_V2_ADD, ERR_R_MALLOC_FAILURE);
+        goto err;
+    }
+
+    p = pp;
+    i2d_ESS_SIGNING_CERT_V2(sc, &p);
+    if ((seq = ASN1_STRING_new()) == NULL || !ASN1_STRING_set(seq, pp, len)) {
+        ESSerr(ESS_F_ESS_SIGNING_CERT_V2_ADD, ERR_R_MALLOC_FAILURE);
+        goto err;
+    }
+
+    OPENSSL_free(pp);
+    pp = NULL;
+    return PKCS7_add_signed_attribute(si,
+                                      NID_id_smime_aa_signingCertificateV2,
+                                      V_ASN1_SEQUENCE, seq);
+ err:
+    ASN1_STRING_free(seq);
+    OPENSSL_free(pp);
+    return 0;
+}

+    STACK_OF(ESS_CERT_ID) *cert_ids;

+ *        hashAlgorithm           AlgorithmIdentifier DEFAULT id-sha256,
+ *        certHash                Hash,
+ *        issuerSerial            IssuerSerial OPTIONAL
+ * }
+ */
+
+struct ESS_cert_id_v2_st {
+    X509_ALGOR *hash_alg;       /* Default: SHA-256 */
+    ASN1_OCTET_STRING *hash;
+    ESS_ISSUER_SERIAL *issuer_serial;
+};
+
+/*-
+ * SigningCertificateV2 ::= SEQUENCE {
+ *        certs                   SEQUENCE OF ESSCertIDv2,
+ *        policies                SEQUENCE OF PolicyInformation OPTIONAL
+ * }
+ */
+
+struct ESS_signing_cert_v2_st {
+    STACK_OF(ESS_CERT_ID_V2) *cert_ids;
+    STACK_OF(POLICYINFO) *policy_info;
+};

+=head1 CAdES Basic Electronic Signature (CAdES-BES)
+
+A CAdES Basic Electronic Signature (CAdES-BES), as defined in the European Standard ETSI EN 319 122-1 V1.1.1, contains:
+
+=over 4
+
+=item *

+

+=item *
+
+An ESS signing-certificate or ESS signing-certificate-v2 attribute, as defined in Enhanced Security Services (ESS), RFC 2634 and RFC 5035.
+An ESS signing-certificate attribute only allows for the use of SHA-1 as a digest algorithm.
+An ESS signing-certificate-v2 attribute allows for the use of any digest algorithm.
+
+=item *
+
+The digital signature value computed on the user data and, when present, on the signed attributes.
+
+Note that currently the B<-cades> option applies only to the B<-sign> operation and is ignored during
+the B<-verify> operation, i.e. the signing certification is not checked during the verification process.
+This feature might be added in a future version.
+
+=back
+

@@ -0,0 +1,45 @@
+=pod
+
+=head1 NAME
+
+CMS_add1_signing_cert, CMS_add1_signing_cert_v2
+- add ESS signing-certificate signed attribute to a
+CMS_SignerInfo data structure
+
+=head1 SYNOPSIS
+
+ #include <openssl/cms.h>
+
+ int CMS_add1_signing_cert(CMS_SignerInfo *si, ESS_SIGNING_CERT *sc);
+
+ int CMS_add1_signing_cert_v2(CMS_SignerInfo *si, ESS_SIGNING_CERT_V2 *sc2);
+
+=head1 DESCRIPTION
+
+CMS_add1_signing_cert() adds an ESS Signing Certificate B<sc> (version 1) signed
+attribute to the CMS_SignerInfo B<si>.
+CMS_add1_signing_cert_v2() adds an ESS Signing Certificate B<sc2> (version 2) signed
+attribute to the CMS_SignerInfo B<si>.
+The ESS Signing Certificate attributes version 1 and 2 are defined in RFC 5035
+which updates Section 5.4 of RFC 2634.
+
+=head1 NOTES
+
+This attribute is mandatory to make a CMS compliant with CAdES-BES
+(European Standard ETSI EN 319 122-1 V1.1.1).
+For a fuller description see L<cms(1)>).
+
+=head1 RETURN VALUES
+
+CMS_add1_signing_cert() and CMS_add1_signing_cert_v2() return 1 if attribute is added or 0 if an error occurred.

findings.message: The functions ESS_SIGNING_CERT_get() and ESS_SIGNING_CERT_V2_get() access the ASN1_TYPE union member 'attr->value.sequence' without first validating that 'attr->type == V_ASN1_SEQUENCE'. The ASN1_TYPE structure is a tagged union where the 'value' member can hold different types (sequence, integer, string, etc.) depending on the 'type' field. When a malformed TimeStamp Response contains an attribute with a type other than V_ASN1_SEQUENCE, accessing attr->value.sequence results in type confusion - the code interprets arbitrary data as a pointer to an ASN1_STRING structure, leading to dereferencing invalid or NULL pointers and causing a denial of service crash.
findings.suggestion: Add type validation before accessing the union member. Check that attr->type == V_ASN1_SEQUENCE before accessing attr->value.sequence. Return NULL if the type does not match.
findings.title: ASN1_TYPE union member accessed without type validation

fix_commit.author: Bob Beck
fix_commit.message: Verify ASN1 object's types before attempting to access them as a particular type

must_cover.reason: Primary location of finding: ASN1_TYPE union member accessed without type validation
Related location for: ASN1_TYPE union member accessed without type validation

ground_truth.root_cause: The ASN1_TYPE structure is a tagged union that can hold various ASN.1 types. The code assumes the returned attribute will always be of type V_ASN1_SEQUENCE and directly accesses the sequence member without validation. This violates safe union access patterns where the discriminator (type field) must be checked before accessing the corresponding union member.

pr_description:
A CAdES Basic Electronic Signature (CAdES-BES) contains, among other
specifications, a collection of  Signing Certificate reference attributes,
stored in the signedData ether as ESS signing-certificate or as
ESS signing-certificate-v2. These are described in detail in Section 5.7.2
of RFC 5126 - CMS Advanced Electronic Signatures (CAdES).

This patch adds support for adding  ESS signing-certificate[-v2] attributes
to CMS signedData. Although it implements only a small part of the RFC, it
is sufficient many cases to enable the `openssl cms` app to create signatures
which comply with legal requirements of some European States (e.g Italy).

Reviewed-by: Richard Levitte <levitte@openssl.org>
Reviewed-by: Matthias St. Pierre <Matthias.St.Pierre@ncp-e.com>
(Merged from https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/7893)
pr_title: crypto/cms: Add support for CAdES Basic Electronic Signatures (CAdES-BES)
release_caveats: Actual Git committer date predates 2021: conflicts with current paper. Recommend explicitly removing/excepting introduction-age cutoff, keeping fixing-date window. | Eligibility uses recorded canonical mainline fix alias; preserve construction fix and canonical fix separately. Independently checked ancestry/date and mapping evidence.

agent_reasoning: The buggy code used `if (inlen < (size_t)(tmp[0] - 4))` which has two flaws: (1) the arithmetic is inverted — the correct test is whether inlen is at least 4 + tmp[0], not whether inlen is less than tmp[0] - 4; (2) if tmp[0] < 4 the subtraction underflows when cast to size_t, making the check always false. Both flaws allow the subsequent memcpy to overread the tmp buffer (up to 8 bytes past its end) and overwrite the out buffer (up to 4 bytes past its end). The fix `if (inlen < 4 + (size_t)tmp[0])` correctly checks that the input buffer holds at least the 4-byte header plus a key of length tmp[0], preventing any out-of-bounds memory access.

fix_commit_message:
kek_unwrap_key(): Fix incorrect check of unwrapped key size

Fixes CVE-2025-9230

The check is off by 8 bytes so it is possible to overread by
up to 8 bytes and overwrite up to 4 bytes.

Reviewed-by: Neil Horman <nhorman@openssl.org>
Reviewed-by: Matt Caswell <matt@openssl.org>
Reviewed-by: Tomas Mraz <tomas@openssl.org>

ground_truth.reason: This PR includes the feature with the fix already applied, so the vulnerability is not present

intro_commit_message: Experimental CMS password based recipient Info support.
pr_description:
This PR adds experimental CMS password-based recipient info (PWRI) support and ensures the key unwrapping logic correctly validates the unwrapped key length before copying it.

In `kek_unwrap_key()`, after decrypting the wrapped key material, the code checks that the input buffer is large enough to contain the 4-byte header plus the key indicated by `tmp[0]`. The correct check is:

```c
if (inlen < 4 + (size_t)tmp[0])
```

This ensures the subsequent `memcpy(out, tmp + 4, *outlen)` always reads within the bounds of the `tmp` buffer and writes within the bounds of the `out` buffer. Without this check, a crafted wrapped key could specify a length that causes reads past the end of `tmp` and writes past the end of `out`.
pr_title: CMS password-based recipient info: fix key unwrap length check
release_caveats: Actual Git committer date predates 2021: conflicts with current paper. Recommend explicitly removing/excepting introduction-age cutoff, keeping fixing-date window.

findings.message: The bounds check `if (inlen < (size_t)(tmp[0] - 4))` in kek_unwrap_key() is logically incorrect and allows out-of-bounds memory access. The check should verify that `inlen >= 4 + tmp[0]` (i.e., the input buffer is large enough to contain the 4-byte header plus the key of length tmp[0]). Instead, the code checks `inlen < tmp[0] - 4`, which is off by 8 bytes. Additionally, if tmp[0] < 4, the subtraction `tmp[0] - 4` underflows when cast to size_t, resulting in a very large value that makes the check always pass. After this flawed check, the code executes `memcpy(out, tmp + 4, *outlen)` where `*outlen = tmp[0]`, which can read up to 8 bytes past the end of the tmp buffer and write up to 4 bytes past the end of the out buffer.
findings.suggestion: Change the bounds check from `if (inlen < (size_t)(tmp[0] - 4))` to `if (inlen < 4 + (size_t)tmp[0])` to properly verify that the input buffer contains the full header plus key data before copying.

ground_truth.root_cause: The bounds check `if (inlen < (size_t)(tmp[0] - 4))` contains two errors: (1) the logic is inverted - it should check if inlen is sufficient to hold 4 header bytes plus tmp[0] key bytes, not if inlen is less than tmp[0] minus 4; (2) if tmp[0] < 4, the subtraction underflows when cast to size_t, making the check ineffective. This allows the subsequent memcpy to read and write beyond buffer boundaries.

agent_reasoning: Merged diff composed mechanically by cherry-picking fix 6bca15039e99 on top of intro fe004a09acdf via git's 3-way merge. Vulnerability (OutOfBoundsRead): The use_proxy() function handles IPv6 addresses enclosed in brackets (e.g., '[::1]') by stripping the brackets using strncpy(). However, strncpy() does not add a NUL terminator when it copies exactly the specified number of bytes. After the strncpy() call, 'server' is reassigned to point to the 'host' buffer, which is not NUL-terminated. When strstr(no_proxy, server) is subsequently called, it reads beyond the bounds of 'host' searching for a NUL terminator, causing an out-of-bounds read. This can trigger a crash leading to Denial of Service. Root cause: The strncpy() function does not NUL-terminate the destination buffer when the source string is at least as long as the specified count. In this case, strncpy(host, server + 1, sl) copies exactly 'sl' bytes (the IPv6 address without brackets), but no NUL terminator is added. The code then uses 'host' as a C string with strstr(), which reads memory beyond the buffer bounds.

findings.message: The use_proxy() function handles IPv6 addresses enclosed in brackets (e.g., '[::1]') by stripping the brackets using strncpy(). However, strncpy() does not add a NUL terminator when it copies exactly the specified number of bytes. After the strncpy() call, 'server' is reassigned to point to the 'host' buffer, which is not NUL-terminated. When strstr(no_proxy, server) is subsequently called, it reads beyond the bounds of 'host' searching for a NUL terminator, causing an out-of-bounds read. This can trigger a crash leading to Denial of Service.

related_locations.description: strstr() call that reads from un-terminated buffer

findings.suggestion: Add explicit NUL terminator after the strncpy() call to ensure the host buffer is properly terminated before being used with string functions like strstr().
findings.title: Missing NUL terminator after strncpy causes out-of-bounds read

fix_commit.author: Tomas Mraz

ground_truth.root_cause: The strncpy() function does not NUL-terminate the destination buffer when the source string is at least as long as the specified count. In this case, strncpy(host, server + 1, sl) copies exactly 'sl' bytes (the IPv6 address without brackets), but no NUL terminator is added. The code then uses 'host' as a C string with strstr(), which reads memory beyond the buffer bounds.

agent_reasoning: Merged diff composed mechanically by cherry-picking fix 61f428a2fc66 on top of intro 055dd1d8bb24 via git's 3-way merge. Vulnerability (OutOfBoundsRead): The partial-block pre-processing code in ossl_aes_cfb128_vaes_enc and ossl_aes_cfb128_vaes_dec unconditionally loads 16 bytes from the input buffer using unmasked vmovdqu8 instructions, even when fewer bytes are valid. When processing partial blocks (where $left contains 1-15 valid bytes), the vmovdqu8 (%r11),%xmm0 and vmovdqu8 ($inp),%xmm1 instructions always load a full 16-byte vector. This can read 1-15 bytes beyond the valid buffer boundary. If the input buffer ends at a memory page boundary and the following page is unmapped, this triggers a crash leading to denial of service. Notably, the post-processing code in the same file correctly uses masked loads with {%k1}{z} to avoid this issue, but this pattern was not consistently applied in the pre-processing section. Root cause: Inconsistent use of masked vs unmasked AVX-512 load instructions. The partial-block pre-processing code path uses unmasked vmovdqu8 loads that always read 16 bytes, while the post-processing code correctly uses masked loads with {%k1}{z}. The mask register k1 is properly initialized with a bitmask for valid bytes, but this mask is not applied to the pre-processing loads.

+.extern  OPENSSL_ia32cap_P

+#################################################################
+# Signature:
+#
+# int ossl_aes_cfb128_vaes_eligible(void);
+#
+# Detects if the underlying hardware supports all the features
+# required to run the Intel AVX-512 implementations of AES-CFB128 algorithms.
+#
+# Returns: non zero if all the required features are detected, 0 otherwise
+#################################################################
+
+.globl   ossl_aes_cfb128_vaes_eligible

+.balign  64

+ossl_aes_cfb128_vaes_eligible:
+.cfi_startproc

+#################################################################
+#

+# - preloading the AES key schedule into AVX registers
+# - single-block AES encryption used by CFB encryption and decryption

+# - VPXORD for AES pre-whitening

+# - VAESENCLAST for performing the last AES encryption round
+#
+# For more information please consult:
+# - the Intel(R) 64 and IA-32 Architectures Optimization Reference Manual,
+# Chapter 21: Cryptography & Finite Field Arithmetic Instructions
+# https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/developer/articles/technical/intel64-and-ia32-architectures-optimization.html
+# - the Intel(R) Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) New Instructions Set Whitepaper

+# expects the key schedule address in $key_original
+sub load_aes_key_schedule_1x() {
+$code.=<<___;
+    vmovdqu8   0($key_original),%xmm17  # schedule  0 whitening
+    vmovdqu8  16($key_original),%xmm18  #           1
+    vmovdqu8  32($key_original),%xmm19  #           2
+    vmovdqu8  48($key_original),%xmm20  #           3
+    vmovdqu8  64($key_original),%xmm21  #           4
+    vmovdqu8  80($key_original),%xmm22  #           5
+    vmovdqu8  96($key_original),%xmm23  #           6
+    vmovdqu8 112($key_original),%xmm24  #           7
+    vmovdqu8 128($key_original),%xmm25  #           8
+    vmovdqu8 144($key_original),%xmm26  #           9
+    vmovdqu8 160($key_original),%xmm27  #          10 last for AES-128
+    vmovdqu8 176($key_original),%xmm28  #          11

+    ja ${label_prefix}_192_256

+    vaesenclast %xmm27,$temp,$temp # last AES-128 encryption round
+    jmp ${label_prefix}_end

+.balign 32
+${label_prefix}_192_256:
+

+
+.balign 32

+___

+#################################################################
+# Signature:
+#
+# void ossl_aes_cfb128_vaes_enc(
+#     const unsigned char *in,
+#     unsigned char *out,
+#     size_t len,
+#     const AES_KEY *ks,
+#     const unsigned char ivec[16],
+#     /*in-out*/ ossl_ssize_t *num);
+#
+# Preconditions:
+# - all pointers are valid (not NULL...)
+# - AES key schedule and rounds in `ks` are precomputed
+#
+# Invariants:
+# - `*num` is between 0 and 15 (inclusive)
+#
+#################################################################
+#
+# The implementation follows closely the encryption half of CRYPTO_cfb128_encrypt:
+# - "pre" step: processes the last bytes of a partial block
+# - "mid" step: processes complete blocks
+# - "post" step: processes the first bytes of a partial block
+#
+# To obtain the next ciphertext block `cipher <N>` from
+# the plaintext block `plain <N>`, the previous ciphertext
+# block `cipher <N-1>` is required as input.
+#
+# The dependency on previous encryption outputs (ciphertexts)
+# makes CFB encryption inherently serial.
+#
+#                  +----+                       +----------+
+#                  | iv |       +---------------> cipher 0 |
+#                  +--+-+       |               +----------+
+#                     |         |                     |
+#                     |         |                     |

fix_commit_message:
Out-of-bounds read in AES-CFB-128 on X86-64 with AVX-512 support

The partial-block pre-processing code in ossl_aes_cfb128_vaes_enc and
ossl_aes_cfb128_vaes_dec unconditionally loads 16 bytes from the input buffer
using unmasked vmovdqu8 instructions, even when fewer bytes are valid.
This can read 1–15 bytes beyond the provided buffer. The post-processing code
in the same file correctly uses masked loads to avoid this issue.

Fixes CVE-2026-28386

+
+$output = $#ARGV >= 0 && $ARGV[$#ARGV] =~ m|\.\w+$| ? pop : undef;
+$flavour = $#ARGV >= 0 && $ARGV[0] !~ m|\.| ? shift : undef;
+

+        =~ /GNU assembler version ([2-9]\.[0-9]+)/) {

+    $avx512vaes = ($1>=14.16);

+        # https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xcode#Xcode_7.0_-_10.x_(since_Free_On-Device_Development)_2
+        # clang 7.0.0 is Apple clang 10.0.1
